# Learning Resources

It's important to us that you can effectively contribute to notifyd even if you lack the experience in the technical stack/architecture. In order to to this, we have curated a list of learning resources that members of the team have leveraged in the past, our hope is that this will help you level up to be an effective contributor to notifyd.


| Name      | type     | Good for   | Link |
|----------|----------|----------|----------|
| Building Event-Driven Microservices | 📖 | Understanding how to build event driven architectures. This book goes into detail about all the different components that you should consider when building and maintaining an EDA. I would recommend this book for getting an general overview of EDA's and how to think in events. | [link](https://www.amazon.co.uk/Building-Event-Driven-Microservices-Leveraging-Organizational/dp/1492057894/ref=sr_1_1?crid=2KD5GG7Q767XZ&dchild=1&keywords=building+event+driven+microservices&qid=1628506523&sprefix=building+event-driven+%2Caps%2C426&sr=8-1), [link](https://learning.oreilly.com/library/view/building-event-driven-microservices/9781492057888/) |
| Go by example | 🔗 | Really good for learning Go. I would recommend it if you want to get up and running with Go quickly. | [link](https://gobyexample.com/) |
| What do you mean by “Event-Driven”? | 🔗 | Useful for understanding and articulating different event patterns | [link](https://martinfowler.com/articles/201701-event-driven.html) |
| Learn Go with Tests | 🔗 | A really nice way to learn Go by being hands on. I love the TDD approach as it allows you to learn about testing as well as the concepts. Go is slightly different in the way it handles mocking for example, it leverages dependency injection much more heavily than other langs. | [link](https://quii.gitbook.io/learn-go-with-tests/) |
| Learning Go: An Idiomatic Approach to Real-World Go Programming | 📖 | If you are learning Go and enjoy reading technical books, buy this book. | [link](https://www.amazon.co.uk/Learning-Go-Idiomatic-Real-World-Programming/dp/1492077216/ref=asc_df_1492077216/?tag=googshopuk-21&linkCode=df0&hvadid=463092568931&hvpos=&hvnetw=g&hvrand=7912822425806038294&hvpone=&hvptwo=&hvqmt=&hvdev=c&hvdvcmdl=&hvlocint=&hvlocphy=9045073&hvtargid=pla-1028299556295&psc=1&th=1&psc=1), [link](https://www.oreilly.com/library/view/learning-go/9781492077206/) |
| Functional options for friendly APIs | 🔗 | A really nice idiom in Go for handling multiple configurations in your APIs | [link](https://dave.cheney.net/2014/10/17/functional-options-for-friendly-apis) |
